Thanks again for the great discussion today. Quick recap and the follow-ups we agreed on from the discovery call:

Recap of requirements:
- Latency targets: p95 <= 200ms (US), p95 <= 220ms (EU), p95 <= 300ms (APAC) for our 2-token incremental responses scenario.
- Throughput: steady state 150 requests/sec with occasional bursts to 250 req/sec for short windows.
- Concurrency: expected active concurrency 40-60 users; peak concurrency ~120 for short bursts.
- Streaming: partial token streaming is required for your user experience on chat flows.
- Data residency: EU customer data for EU users must remain in EU; APAC data residency preferred but we can discuss regional routing options.

Attachments: I am sharing our SLO matrix and a draft mutual action plan for procurement and technical deep dive.

1) Can you confirm whether the EU data residency requirement is for all logs and telemetry or just PII and stored documents?
2) Do you expect real-time fan-out to other downstream services in APAC that would require additional routing constraints?
3) Preferred time for the technical deep-dive with your platform team next week (Aditya to lead).

We can meet the numbers we discussed in hosted mode for evaluation, and we will outline Dedicated and multi-region deployment options in the deep-dive. Aditya, putting you on the thread to help with the technical design.

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:15 AM PST
Subject: Re: Performance SLO & Multi-region Routing - follow-up

Michael, Marissa,

Thanks for the note. Quick technical clarifications from our side:

1) Measurement point: our quoted p95 numbers are measured end-to-end from the Redwood API ingress to final token emission to the SDK (network time to client excluded). In practice, client-to-Redwood adds variable network RTT. For sizing recommendations we account for an extra 20-40ms median network RTT inside US/EU and 60-120ms for APAC.

2) Throughput and concurrency: the configuration we recommend for your workload (150 req/s sustained, 250 req/s burst) is achievable with either:
   - Hosted multi-region with regional model replicas and smart routing (recommended for faster time-to-value). We can pin EU traffic to EU replicas for residency.
   - Dedicated capacity with regional reservations if you need predictable isolation and throughput SLAs.

3) Streaming: supported in both modes. Our streaming path keeps the model KV cache warm and emits token deltas as they are generated. For your p95 targets when streaming, expect ~10-20ms additional CPU overhead per token for the streaming serialization path; we account for that in the p95 budgets.

4) Regional routing and fallbacks: we can configure request routing by IP or token indicating region. For strict EU residency, you can opt to block any routing to non-EU regions for EU users; logs and persisted data will be stored in EU-only buckets and audited. For APAC we can route to nearest region but provide an option to keep payloads in APAC-only storage.

5) Benchmarks and margin: based on our internal tests on A100-class hosts, a single Regional replica can sustain ~120-160 req/s for your configured model with 60 concurrent sessions while keeping p95 under 200-220ms for short contexts (<= 512 tokens). For APAC replication we see ~15-30% higher tail latencies depending on region. We'll provide the detailed benchmark PDF in the drive link.

Suggested next steps before the deep-dive:
- We will prepare a short runbook showing hosted vs dedicated latency/price tradeoffs (Aditya).
- Marissa will send a draft Mutual Action Plan and proposed times.
- Michael/Priya to confirm whether audit logs must be encrypted with customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM).

Happy to run a quick perf test with a small pilot if you want to validate the streaming p95 with your client.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
